description: InverseVIsTraffic is a Julia and Python research codebase for estimating traffic-network relationships through inverse variational inequalities. Its README describes estimating user cost or travel latency functions and origin-destination demand for an Eastern Massachusetts road application. Users need a network, travel observations and optimisation settings; outputs are fitted demand or cost parameters for the chosen traffic case. Geographic coverage of the published application is Eastern Massachusetts, but the method can be applied to other supplied networks. The README explicitly grants MIT terms for the code. A material limitation is that the raw INRIX measurements used by the authors are confidential, so the published results cannot be fully reproduced from this repository alone. The README links a separate public Eastern Massachusetts benchmark network. This model can help calibrate congestion assumptions in road-infrastructure simulation. The related catalogue AequilibraE record is a different transport modelling package. No road dataset or software was downloaded.
inputs: Road network, observed traffic and inference settings
name: InverseVIsTraffic road-network inference
notes: G7 G7-1701. Prepared draft only. Metadata review on 2026-09-28; no models, data or archives downloaded. Related-resource comparisons are reviewer mappings, not tested interoperability. Raw INRIX data are confidential; public benchmark network is linked separately.
outputs: Estimated demand and travel-latency cost functions
